=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/ai_memory_lib.py
  Line or code reference: _build_scope (lines 520-531)
  Problem: The simplified `_build_scope` no longer clears out-of-scope fields when resolving the scope level. When `run_id` is truthy (level="run"), `issue_number` and `pr_number` remain set from caller context instead of being nullified. When `issue_number` is set but `run_id` is not (level="task"), `run_id` remains set if the caller passed one. The old code explicitly nullified these fields per level.
  Why it fails at runtime: Records can carry contradictory scope metadata — e.g., a "run"-scoped record with a non-None `issue_number` from an outer caller context. Downstream retrieval logic that keys on scope shape will mis-match or skip records.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/memory_helpers.sh
  Line or code reference: removed lines 45-136 (memory_bootstrap and _memory_bootstrap_define_fallback)
  Problem: `memory_bootstrap` is removed but is actively called by plan.yml:555,873, review_autofix.yml:1617,1718, implement.yml:1500,1680, clarify.yml:510,666, and validate.yml:607,903,1023. Seven distinct workflow files invoke it. While clarify.yml:494-509 has a defensive `declare -F` wrapper that defines a no-op fallback, plan.yml:555 calls `memory_bootstrap --ensure-branch` without any such guard, and implement.yml:1500 calls it unconditionally.
  Why it fails at runtime: When any unguarded workflow step reaches `memory_bootstrap`, the shell will fail with "memory_bootstrap: command not found" and exit non-zero (all these workflows use `set -euo pipefail`). This hard-breaks plan, implement, and validate workflows.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/tg_helpers.sh
  Line or code reference: removed lines 289-307 (tg_send_phase_failure)
  Problem: `tg_send_phase_failure` is removed but called unconditionally by clarify.yml:1307, plan.yml:2125, review_autofix.yml:5503. implement.yml:4913 guards with `declare -F` and would silently skip, but the other three callers have no guard.
  Why it fails at runtime: When clarify, plan, or review_autofix hits its failure-notification path and invokes `tg_send_phase_failure`, the shell fails with "command not found" and exits non-zero, turning a notification failure into a workflow hard-failure.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/ai_memory.py
  Line or code reference: removed lines 1955-1959 (--category, --scope-level, --max CLI args from retrieve subparser), removed lines 1988 (--scope-level from record-candidate subparser)
  Problem: `plan.yml:884-891` and `clarify.yml:677-684` both call `memory_retrieve ... --category "repo_learnings" --scope-level "global" --max "10"`. The `memory_retrieve` shell wrapper passes all arguments through to `ai_memory.py retrieve`. With these CLI flags removed, argparse will reject them as unrecognized arguments and exit(2).
  Why it fails at runtime: Every plan and clarify run that reaches the memory-retrieval step will fail with argparse error before any retrieval logic executes. The `memory_retrieve` wrapper does not catch exit code 2 differently from other failures.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/ai_memory_lib.py
  Line or code reference: line 68 (repo_learnings removed from ALLOWED_CATEGORIES)
  Problem: `memory_maintenance.yml:357` calls `memory_record_candidate --category "repo_learnings"`. `record_candidate` at line 1565 validates `normalized_category not in ALLOWED_CATEGORIES` and raises `MemoryValidationError("Unsupported memory category: repo_learnings")`. The shell wrapper `memory_record_candidate` treats non-zero exit as fail-open, so the workflow won't hard-fail, but every `repo_learnings` write is silently dropped.
  Why it fails at runtime: The repo-learnings memory pipeline in memory_maintenance.yml, plan.yml, and clarify.yml silently stops producing records. No error surfaces in CI, but the data pipeline is broken.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: tests/test_memory_record_schema.py
  Line or code reference: line 80, function test_build_scope_treats_blank_override_as_unset
  Problem: The test calls `ai_memory_lib._build_scope(42, None, None, "   ")` with 4 positional arguments, but the PR reduced `_build_scope`'s signature to 3 parameters `(issue_number, pr_number, run_id)`. The fourth argument `"   "` was the `scope_level_override` parameter that was removed.
  Why it fails at runtime: CI at ci.yml:393 runs `python3 tests/test_memory_record_schema.py`. This test raises `TypeError: _build_scope() takes 3 positional arguments but 4 were given` and fails CI.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
